newsitem.title: BELARUS: Yeltsin, Lukashenko discuss Belarus crisis by phone.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin, Lukashenko discuss Belarus crisis by phone.

text.p: President Alexander Lukashenko, locked in a political standoff with his parliament, spoke by telephone with Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Wednesday, the Belarussian leader's top aide told Reuters.

"He is speaking to Yeltsin right now, " Vladimir Zametalin said. He had no further information on the conversation or whether Lukashenko would agree to attend peace talks later in the day in the Russian town of Smolensk.
The telephone conversation with Yeltsin, still recovering in hospital from heart surgery two weeks ago, followed Russian moves on Tuesday to defuse the crisis between Lukashenko and his critics.

Tension has been rising in Belarus over Lukashenko's plans to extend his powers in a referendum on November 24. Belarussian parliament speaker Semyon Sharetsky said on Wednesday he planned to go to Smolensk, halfway between Minsk and Moscow, for talks with Russian leaders later in the day.

Yeltsin and Chernomyrdin said on Tuesday they were alarmed by the conflict in Belarus and urged a compromise. Lukashenko's aides said he had yet to decide whether to attend the Smolensk talks, expected to include Chernomyrdin and the speakers of both houses of the Russian parliament.
Sharetsky has accused Lukashenko of planning to introduce a dictatorship.
